source.title: Which Mutual-Information Representation Learning Objectives are Sufficient for Control?
source.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34 (NeurIPS 2021)

confidence_rationale: The single most on-point formal treatment of SD-106's objective choice, and it splits rather than settles. It proves that a GENERIC predictive objective (forward information) IS sufficient to represent optimal Q-functions for any reward function -- which defends genericity per se and is the reason this entry is not a bare 'weakens' -- while stating in the same breath that such a representation 'lacks a notion of task-relevance as it must be equally predictive of all predictable elements in the state'. That second half is exactly SD-106's regime. Confidence is held to 0.72 by two real gaps: the paper analyses mutual-information objectives, and reconstruction/FVU is NOT among the objectives it proves on (it is raised only as a conjecture about the ELBO in discussion); and its sufficiency notion is information-theoretic, i.e. capacity-unbounded, whereas SD-106's whole difficulty is a 32-dimensional bound.
failure_signatures: The paper's sufficiency results are capacity-unbounded: they ask whether a representation RETAINS the information needed to represent the optimal policy, not whether a FIXED-WIDTH code spends its dimensions on the right directions. SD-106 is near its own PCA-32 ceiling (0.951-0.980), so its deficit cannot be an information-retention failure of the kind these propositions rule on -- it is an allocation failure the propositions are silent about.

Reconstruction is not analysed. Transferring the J_fwd task-relevance remark to SD-106's FVU-with-linear-decoder objective is an argument by family resemblance, not an instance of the paper's theorem. If anything reconstruction is WEAKER than J_fwd here: it is predictive of the observation rather than of the dynamics, so a direction can be reconstructible and dynamically inert.

The result cuts against an over-quick 'generic objectives are simply wrong' reading: J_fwd is proved SUFFICIENT and two of the more task-shaped objectives (state-only transition information, inverse information) are proved INSUFFICIENT. Task-conditioning is therefore not automatically an improvement -- an inverse-model or reward-only successor to SD-106 could be strictly worse on this paper's own analysis.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Formalising sufficiency of a state representation for learning and representing the optimal policy, the paper proves that forward information (J_fwd) is sufficient for all reward functions, while state-only transition information (J_state) and inverse information (J_inv) are not -- 'given mild and common assumptions on the structure of the MDP'. It then notes: 'Of the objectives studied in our analysis, only J_fwd is sufficient to represent optimal Q-functions for any reward function. Note however that the representation obtained by this objective lacks a notion of task-relevance as it must be equally predictive of all predictable elements in the state.'
mapping.ree_translation: REE reads the second sentence as the formal name for SD-106's measured situation. SD-106 optimises a task-agnostic scale-normalised reconstruction term and, per V3-EXQ-1041, achieves 0.951-0.980 of the achievable PCA-32 ceiling -- it is being 'equally predictive of all predictable elements' close to optimally. The objective therefore has no lever by which to prefer decision-relevant directions, and under a 32-dimensional bound the retained directions are ordered by variance rather than by consumer relevance. That is a precise candidate mechanism for the consumer-rung shortfall (0.719 oracle-action agreement against a 0.85 bar) that does NOT require the encoder to be under-trained or the mechanism to be defective. The paper equally warns REE off the naive fix: two of the more obviously task-shaped objectives it studies are the ones proved insufficient.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Two boundaries, both load-bearing. (1) Sufficiency here is information-theoretic and capacity-unbounded; SD-106's deficit is an allocation problem inside a fixed 32-dim code, which no proposition in this paper addresses. The transfer is from the paper's informal task-relevance REMARK, not from its theorems. (2) Reconstruction/FVU is not one of the analysed objectives -- the paper only conjectures in discussion that the ELBO alone cannot sufficiently control representation content -- so applying the J_fwd remark to SD-106's objective is an argument from the same family, not a derivation. Additionally the analysis is over MDPs with a reward function, whereas SD-106's consumer rung is measured as agreement with an oracle ACTION, which is a related but not identical target.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical analysis with proofs over MDP structure, corroborated on a simulated game environment with visual observations; machine-learning representation-learning literature, no biological data.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: a NeurIPS paper whose central contributions are proofs, with explicit counterexamples and stated assumptions, from a group central to this literature. Mapping fidelity is the limiting component and is deliberately below 0.7: the sentence REE leans on is an acknowledged limitation in the paper's discussion rather than one of its results, and the objective SD-106 actually ships is not among those proved on. Transfer risk moderate rather than high because the structural correspondence is unusually tight -- a bounded latent trained by a task-agnostic predictive objective, read by a downstream control consumer, is the paper's own setting.
